classification.difficultyReason: Source Mastery question requiring square side lengths to be recovered from areas and shared boundaries to be excluded from the perimeter.

content.prompt: Three squares are joined together to form a shape. Calculate the perimeter of the entire shape.

spec.description: Three unfilled adjoining squares increase in size from left to right, share a horizontal bottom baseline and form a stepped exterior.
spec.mathematics: The square areas are 36 cm², 64 cm² and 81 cm². The coordinate side lengths are derived from those areas without printing the resulting lengths. Shared vertical boundaries are dashed; exterior step edges are solid.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied area labels are visible.

answer.short: $64\text{ cm}$. Square sides are $6,8,9\text{ cm}$; add the exterior edges.
answer.worked:
Using $A=l^2$, find each square's side length.
$$\begin{align*}l_1^2&=36\\l_1&=6\text{ cm}\\l_2^2&=64\\l_2&=8\text{ cm}\\l_3^2&=81\\l_3&=9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The bottom edge is $6+8+9=23\text{ cm}$; the exposed steps are $9-8=1\text{ cm}$ and $8-6=2\text{ cm}$. Add the exterior edges clockwise from the bottom.
$$\begin{align*}P&=23+9+9+1+8+2+6+6\\P&=64\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
